spec: The living chronicle (sim/chronicle.ts): what happens in play becomes history people retell, through the same voice as the old beats (history-voice.ts). Each kind has summary templates (one is picked per event, seeded) and a gist (the noun phrase a dawn line uses). Slots: {name} the person, {town} the town, {heir}, {doctrine}, {challenger}, {incumbent}, {event}, {age}. keep = how many entries of each kind live at once (oldest of that kind drop out, so a run of happenings cannot push out a death); onlyFirstPerPerson = kinds recorded once per key (a second reignite of the same person, or the same happening in the same town, is not news). events = how each happening is named in a sentence. keepByKind = a kind's own keep where it differs (civic history: every generated town writes its backstory at founding). Civic kinds (sim/chronicle chronicleCivic): raised (a building went up; {building}, {when}, {owner}) and tier (a town grew; {tier}, {when}). rival: a rival creed rose against the seat's creed (doctrine-dissent, juice doctrine.rival; {challenger}, {incumbent}, {town} where it rose).

summaries: Folk in {town} had had enough of the {incumbent}. One spring they started meeting under the {challenger} instead.
The {challenger} began in {town}, in a back room, with people who had stopped believing the {incumbent}.
Nobody remembers who first spoke for the {challenger} in {town}. Everyone remembers the {incumbent} did not like it.

reignite.gist: the day {name} came back to life
summaries: {name} had gone grey as ash, and then one day in {town} they were laughing again. Nobody knows quite what did it.
Everyone had given up on {name}. Then a stranger kept coming by, and the fire took again.
{name} sat by a cold hearth in {town} for a season. Now you can't keep them indoors.
They say it was a small thing that brought {name} back. Someone just kept showing up.
{name} was laid to rest in {town}. Half the place came out, more than you'd think.
We buried {name} at {age}. The house still sounds wrong without them.
{name} went quiet in the night, in {town}. Someone kept the lamp lit till morning.
The {doctrine} fell apart in {town}. The notices came down in a day, and nobody admitted they'd believed it.
For a while everyone in {town} swore by the {doctrine}. Then it promised one thing too many.
The {doctrine} went the way of all such things in {town}: loud, then quiet, then gone.
In {town} the {challenger} pushed the {incumbent} aside. Same promises, new paint.
The {incumbent} lost {town} to the {challenger}. People still argue whether anything changed.
The one who carried the spark burned out at last. {heir} took it up, and kept walking.
When the old carrier's fire went out, it was {heir} who stood up. Nobody asked them to.
There was a carrier before {heir}. You can see some of them in how {heir} listens.
{event} came to {town}. Folk still date things by it: before, and after.
Remember {event}? {town} talked of nothing else for weeks.
That was the season of {event} in {town}. Odd days.
Someone had coin buried out by {town}. One morning the hole was empty, and nobody said a word.
A hidden purse near {town} went walking. Everyone looked at everyone else for a month.
A patron made fine promises in {town}, then turned on the one who trusted them. It was talked about for a long while.
Never shake hands with a patron, they say in {town}. They have a story to go with it.
The {building} at {town} went up {when}. {owner} carried the first stones.
{owner} raised the {building} in {town} {when}. It has stood ever since.
They say the {building} at {town} went up {when}, and nobody has agreed about the roof since.
{town} was a scatter of roofs once. It became a {tier} {when}.
Nobody voted on it, but {town} was a {tier} {when}. You could tell by the noise.

rival: A creed that stops listening grows a rival.
Every old sign has a new one painted behind it.
reignite: Makes you think anybody could come back.
death: Light a candle if you pass the stone.
We say their name at the hearth still.
collapse: Don't trust a notice that promises bread.
Folk are slower to believe now.
swap: Watch who's painting the next sign.
succession: The spark doesn't die with the hand that held it.
happening: I don't expect we'll see the like again.
theft: Bury it deeper, is the lesson.
betrayal: Promises from the city weigh nothing.
raised: Somebody built it. Somebody always does.
Walk past it and you can still see the mason's marks.
tier: Places grow when nobody is watching.
The old ones still call it the hamlet.
